description: Sayadieh Fish Rice is a beloved Middle Eastern seafood dish featuring flaky fish, aromatic rice, and sweet caramelized onions. This traditional recipe creates a harmonious blend of savory and sweet, making it a perfect meal for family gatherings or a special dinner. Its rich flavors and comforting textures are a true taste of the Levant.

instructions.title: Prepare the Caramelized Onions
instructions.text: Heat 1/4 cup of vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until they turn a deep golden brown and are beautifully caramelized. Remove about half of the caramelized onions and set aside for garnish.

instructions.title: Create the Onion Broth
instructions.text: To the remaining onions in the pot, add 3 cups of warm fish broth or water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to infuse the liquid with the onion flavor. Strain the broth, pressing the onions to extract all liquid, and discard the solids. This is your flavorful onion broth.

instructions.title: Season and Fry the Fish
instructions.text: Pat the fish fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and 1 tablespoon of the Sayadieh spice mix. In a large frying pan, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Fry the fish fillets for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Set aside.

instructions.title: Cook the Aromatic Rice
instructions.text: In the same pot used for the onions (or a clean one), add the rinsed and drained rice. Pour in the prepared onion broth. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of Sayadieh spice mix, turmeric, and season with salt to taste. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

instructions.title: Assemble the Sayadieh
instructions.text: Once the rice is cooked, gently fluff it with a fork. You can either layer the fish on top of the rice in the pot and let it warm through for a few minutes, or serve the rice on a large platter and arrange the fish fillets over it. The choice is yours for presentation.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Garnish the Sayadieh generously with the reserved caramelized onions, toasted pine nuts, and freshly chopped parsley. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for a burst of citrus flavor. Enjoy this authentic Middle Eastern delight!

tips: Achieve truly deep caramelized onions by cooking them slowly over medium-low heat. Patience is key for their rich color and sweet flavor.
For an extra layer of flavor, you can pan-fry the fish bones and heads (if available) before making the broth. This adds depth to your onion-infused liquid.
Sayadieh is excellent served with a simple cucumber and tomato salad or a dollop of plain yogurt to balance the rich flavors.
